newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends lower on pork export ban.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends lower on pork export ban.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar finished lower on Friday on news that Taiwan had announced a temporary ban on exports of fresh and frozen pork due to an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease.
The local unit ended at T$27.537 against Thursday's T$27.524 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$291 million.
"The pork export ban will reduce our overall exports by some 1.5 percent, thus cutting our trade surplus and adding pressure on the Taiwan dollar to fall," said one dealer.
Taiwan's pork exports totalled US$1.55 billion in 1996, 99.48 percent of which went to Japan, the Board of Foreign Trade said on Friday.
The pork exports represented 1.34 percent of the island's total exports, which totalled US$115.98 billion in 1996.
Dealers also attributed the local dollar depreciation to quarter-end U.S. dollar demand and a response to the strength of the U.S. dollar overseas.
"I would say the emerging U.S. dollar demand was a major factor in Friday's trading, while the pork news had a psychological impact," said another dealer.
However, dealers noted persistent foreign fund inflows for the boosting stock market, which would offset any major Taiwan dollar drepreciation.
"Taking the persistent inflows of foreign equity funds into account, the Taiwan dollar should continue its recent narrow-range trading around the current levels," the second dealer said.
For next week, a T$27.50-27.55 range was seen.
